author_notes: Repo-grounded static animated ceramics-grid Edit/state_continuity task hardened to a true-new-L4 with the grid's own genre-native lever. The reference (a) adds the catalog's 'Firing collection' browse control above the grid - kiln-process tabs (All / Anagama / Ash glaze / Reduction / Salt & soda) with a live count readout - and echoes the same 'Firing collection' wordmark mark in the masthead intro, grid footer and related footer in the warm-clay palette, (b) repairs the process-tab row mobile overflow (fixed nowrap row -> wrapping flex tabs), and (c) wires the filter so clicking a process filters the ten ceramic cards and #coll-readout reflects the live count. The bad 'smart-wrong' solution narrows the tab row to 560px + a phantom overflow-x:hidden on the readout only (document still overflows the 390px viewport -> D6 fail), echoes the collection mark in the grid footer only (D2 cross-section fail on the intro + related mark), collapses the ceramic grid into a shingled overlapping pile with a near-black-on-near-black illegible active tab (D3 visual_regression fail on non-empty crops - genuinely broken layout, not a recolor), and flips the active tab while re-asserting a frozen 'Showing all 10 pieces' snapshot that never filters the grid (click succeeds but the terminal readout + grid stay stale -> D4 interaction_assertions fail). It fails FOUR distinct gates while all text / completion / regression / console signals pass. The image and svg assets (img/1.png .. img/10.png, sponsor artwork) are preserved from the original repo.
design_constraints: Echo the SAME 'Firing collection' mark in the masthead intro, the grid footer and the related/notes footer so the collection framing is consistent throughout; do not place it in only one section.
Fix the responsive layout of the process-tab row so it wraps or shrinks within a 390px viewport; do not delete the filter, change the five process tabs, or restyle unrelated sections.

Preserve the ceramics design language: warm clay ground, Playfair Display titles, product artwork emphasis, anime.js transitions and the original detail overlay; the filter and the grid must render in the warm-clay palette with legible tabs, not a dark-on-dark or overlapping layout.
Keep the filter wired end to end (clicking a process tab filters the grid and the #coll-readout count reflects the selection), not merely an active-tab class toggle.
Do not introduce external stylesheets, remote fonts, CDNs, or new remote script/asset dependencies; the site must stay a self-contained static build with a clean console.

change_completion: The 'Firing collection' filter (process tabs + live count) sits above the grid and the mark echoes in the masthead intro, grid footer and related footer.
The process-tab row renders within the viewport on mobile.
Clicking a process tab filters the grid and updates the #coll-readout count to the chosen process.
design_consistency: The warm-clay palette, wordmark, product-artwork rhythm and detail overlay are preserved.
The filter control keeps the warm-clay look with legible tabs and is visually faithful to the reference across the three sections.
regression: The animated grid, ten ceramic cards, detail overlay, magnifier and Close control remain reachable and unchanged.
The static site serves from index.html with a clean browser console.
responsive: 390px homepage (initial, filter bar, intro mark) and 834px tablet have no horizontal overflow beyond 24px.
The process tabs wrap or shrink cleanly instead of forcing a fixed-width non-wrapping row.

metadata.source_repo_kind: Static Codrops expanding product-grid animation with product cards, Details/Item JavaScript classes, anime.js transitions, image zoom, close/return flow, sponsor surface, and product/related image assets.

problem_statement: codrops/ExpandingGridItemAnimation is a no-build static animated product grid, restyled as 'Kiln & Cinder' - a wood-fired ceramics studio catalog curated by Roan Emberly, with a Playfair Display wordmark over a warm clay ground, a grid of ten ceramic pieces (Ember Vessel, Ash Bloom Bowl, ...) that keep the original img/1.png through img/10.png artwork, and the original click-to-open detail overlay with anime.js transitions, artwork zoom (magnifier), and close-back-to-grid. Deliver three coordinated things while preserving the ceramics visual system: (1) Add the catalog's own 'Firing collection' browse control directly above the grid - a row of kiln-process tabs (All / Anagama / Ash glaze / Reduction / Salt & soda) with a live count readout ('Showing all 10 pieces', and after a filter 'Showing 3 of 10 pieces . Anagama'). Give each of the ten pieces its firing category, and echo the same 'Firing collection' wordmark mark in the masthead intro, the grid footer AND the related/notes footer so the collection framing is consistent throughout - the same mark in all three sections, styled in the quiet warm-clay language (light surface, restrained ember accents), visually faithful to the reference and not a collapsed or illegible layout. (2) REPAIR the process-tab row so it stays within the viewport on a 390px phone with no horizontal overflow (the naive layout is a fixed-width non-wrapping row that pushes the whole page sideways); do not merely clip it with overflow-x:hidden - the document itself must not exceed the mobile viewport width. (3) Wire the filter end to end: clicking a process tab must filter the grid to the pieces of that firing AND update the '#coll-readout' count to reflect the selection (e.g. Anagama sets 'Showing 3 of 10 pieces . Anagama') - the post-click terminal state must reflect the chosen process, not the default 'Showing all 10 pieces'. Keep the animated grid, all ten ceramic cards with their titles + makers, the detail overlay with its anime.js transitions, Add to cart / close / magnifier controls, sponsor and related surfaces, and the desktop/tablet layout intact.
required_content: A 'Firing collection' browse control sits directly above the grid: kiln-process tabs (All / Anagama / Ash glaze / Reduction / Salt & soda) and a live count readout that starts at 'Showing all 10 pieces'.
The same 'Firing collection' mark echoes in the masthead intro, the grid footer AND the related/notes footer - the collection framing appears in all three sections, not only one.

The filter control keeps the warm-clay ceramics look (light surface, restrained ember accents, legible tabs) and is visually faithful to the reference rendering - not a collapsed, overlapping, or illegible layout.
The process-tab row renders within the viewport on a 390px phone with no horizontal document overflow beyond 24px.

The filter is wired end to end: clicking a process tab filters the grid to that firing and updates '#coll-readout' to a live count (e.g. Anagama sets 'Showing 3 of 10 pieces . Anagama'); the post-click terminal state reflects the chosen process, not the default 'Showing all 10 pieces'.
The desktop (1440px) and tablet (834px) layouts stay within their viewports.

The animated grid, all ten ceramic cards (titles + makers), the click-to-open detail overlay with its anime.js transitions, artwork zoom (magnifier), Add to cart / close controls, and the Kiln & Cinder wordmark remain reachable and unchanged, and the static site keeps a clean browser console (no remote CDN/font errors).
state_constraints: desktop_initial, tablet_initial, and mobile_initial protect the product grid, sponsor area, added state surface, and responsive layout before any interaction.
desktop_marble_open protects the first product's detail overlay, Add to cart button, close button, magnifier control, product image, and Marble Dream status text.
desktop_marble_zoom protects the magnifier transition and the zoom-focus status while retaining a usable close control.
desktop_marble_closed protects the return-to-grid state after opening and closing Marble Dream, including the original product order.
desktop_space_open protects that the same status system works for a second product rather than being hard-coded only for the first card.
mobile_marble_open protects the state-aware detail overlay and readable text at 390px mobile.
